_about: Flagship facts for Great Smoky Mountains, carried over from the Parkday Smokies research report (2026-11-14) and rechecked against NPS.gov on 2026-11-19. 'official' rows were checked against an NPS page or the Smokies Guide park newspaper. 'approximate' rows are estimates and must never be shown as fact. Closures change weekly: the page always links to the live NPS closures page.

sources.title: NPS: Current road, trail and facility closures

preTrip.label: official
preTrip.text: Buy a parking tag before you drive in. Any stop longer than 15 minutes needs one, and most trailheads have no tag machine.

preTrip.label: official
preTrip.text: There is no gas, EV charging, showers or restaurant inside the park. Visitor centers and camp stores sell limited food.

preTrip.label: official
preTrip.text: Cell service is not guaranteed across large parts of the park. Download maps and your itinerary before you leave town. In an emergency call 911.

preTrip.label: official
preTrip.text: Pets are allowed only on the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail, plus campgrounds and roadsides, on a leash of six feet or less.

preTrip.label: official
preTrip.text: Stay at least 25 yards from elk and never feed wildlife. Feeding wildlife carries a fine.

reservations.label: official
reservations.name: Cades Cove vehicle-free Wednesdays
reservations.text: The loop road closes to cars on Wednesdays from May 6 to Sept. 30 (2026 dates). Bikes can be rented at the campground store.

reservations.label: official
reservations.name: Synchronous fireflies at Elkmont
reservations.text: Viewing runs in late May (May 20 to 27 in 2026) and needs a vehicle pass won through a Recreation.gov lottery held in April.

reservations.label: official
reservations.name: Backcountry camping
reservations.text: Every overnight in the backcountry needs a permit.

reservations.label: official
reservations.name: LeConte Lodge
reservations.text: The only lodging inside the park. It is reached only on foot and needs a reservation.

seasonalRoads.note: Dates are the 2026 season from the NPS seasonal road schedule. 2027 dates are not published yet.

rows.road: Cades Cove Loop, Cataloochee Road, Upper Tremont Road, Wear Cove Road

rows.close: Closes for snow and ice with little notice

closures.label: official
closures.name: Laurel Falls Trail
closures.text: Closed for rehabilitation of the lower viewing area. Reopening is expected in 2027. The park suggests Little River Trail to Huskey Branch Falls, the Deep Creek waterfalls loop or Hen Wallow Falls instead.

closures.label: official
closures.name: Mingus Mill
closures.text: Temporarily closed for preservation work, with no reopening date.

closures.label: official
closures.name: Carlos Campbell Overlook
closures.text: Temporarily closed on Newfound Gap Road.

closures.label: official
closures.name: Big Creek and Cataloochee trails
closures.text: Hurricane Helene damage: Big Creek Trail is open only to Mouse Creek Falls, Caldwell Fork is closed beyond the Boogerman junction, and several other trails are closed or not advised.

closures.label: official
closures.name: Abrams Falls Trail
closures.text: Was closed through Sept. 30, 2026 for footlog replacement. Confirm it has reopened before you plan on it.

closures.label: official
closures.name: Caves and mine shafts
closures.text: All entry is prohibited to protect bats from white-nose syndrome.

visitorCenters.name: Sugarlands Visitor Center
visitorCenters.where: Tennessee, just south of Gatlinburg on Newfound Gap Road
visitorCenters.services: Exhibits, film, park store, parking tags (staffed and a 24-hour machine), accessible restrooms, free all-terrain wheelchair checkout

visitorCenters.name: Oconaluftee Visitor Center
visitorCenters.where: North Carolina, just north of Cherokee on US-441
visitorCenters.services: Exhibits, park store, Mountain Farm Museum next door, elk often in the nearby fields, accessible restrooms, free all-terrain wheelchair checkout

visitorCenters.name: Cades Cove Visitor Center
visitorCenters.where: Midway around the Cades Cove Loop at the Cable Mill
visitorCenters.services: Historic mill area, park store, accessible restrooms

visitorCenters.name: Kuwohi Visitor Contact Station
visitorCenters.where: End of Kuwohi Road, open only while the road is open

visitorCenters.name: Great Smoky Mountains Institute at Tremont
visitorCenters.where: Tremont Road off Laurel Creek Road

partnerCenters: Gatlinburg Welcome Center, the Great Smokies Welcome Center in Townsend and the Swain County Visitor Center in Bryson City are outside the park and also sell parking tags.

seasons.good: Wildflowers along Porters Creek and Kephart Prong, waterfalls at high flow, synchronous fireflies in late May.
seasons.watch: Seasonal roads open on different dates, and cold snaps hit the high ridges.

seasons.good: Every seasonal road is open, ranger programs run, and Cades Cove is car-free on Wednesdays.
seasons.watch: Peak crowds, haze, afternoon thunderstorms and trailhead lots full by mid-morning.

seasons.good: Leaf color starts on the high ridges and works down, and elk rut in Cataloochee and Oconaluftee.
seasons.watch: The heaviest traffic of the year on October weekends. Kuwohi Road and Roaring Fork close on Nov. 29.

seasons.good: Quiet trails, snow on the high ridges and lower lodging prices in the gateway towns.
seasons.watch: Newfound Gap Road can close for ice, and Kuwohi Road, Roaring Fork and several other roads are closed until spring.

accessibility.label: official
accessibility.text: Free all-terrain wheelchairs can be checked out at Sugarlands and Oconaluftee visitor centers for approved trails. A companion is required and checkout is booked in advance through the park.

accessibility.label: official
accessibility.text: Sugarlands, Oconaluftee and Cades Cove visitor centers have accessible restrooms.

accessibility.label: approximate
accessibility.text: Drive-based scenery: Cades Cove Loop, Newfound Gap Road, the Foothills Parkway, and Roaring Fork in season.

accessibility.label: approximate
accessibility.text: Flatter paths: the Mountain Farm Museum, the Oconaluftee River Trail and the Sugarlands nature trail. Confirm surfaces with the park.

accessibility.label: approximate
accessibility.text: The paved path to the Kuwohi tower is short but very steep and is not suitable for most wheelchair users without help.
